prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the camera wearer's transition from an office room in frames 1–3 out through a narrow doorway and hallway in frames 4–5, showing a continuous floor plane and receding walls from roughly 0.3 m to 5 m away. In frame 1, the bright foreground silhouette places the dog and adjacent white box at the lower left within about 1–1.2 m (near the camera wearer's reach), separated by roughly 1.5 m from a wooden chair and left desk behind them (2–3 m away) and a person seated at a right-hand desk about 2–2.5 m away whose outstretched arm is within reach of the desk surface and potted plant. Across frames 2 and 3, the dog and left furniture leave the field of view as the camera wearer turns right and retreats to about 2.5–3 m from the seated person, whose head turns toward the camera in frame 3 while their body remains angled toward the desk monitors; in frames 4 and 5, bright vertical walls and doorframes on the left and right pass within 0.3–0.8 m (well within arm's reach) occluding the office behind, while the hallway opens to a distant room 4–5 m ahead. The depth map clearly reveals the 3D contour of the seated person, desk, chair, and potted plant in frame 3 where extreme backlighting makes the RGB foreground nearly pitch black, as well as the close proximity of the dark doorway walls in frames 4–5. However, the map is unreliable around overexposed windowpanes in frames 2–3 (rendering outdoor views at the same mid-depth as indoor walls), blurs the seated person and office chair into a single merged mass, and flattens the distant room in frames 4–5 into a uniform black void.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a sparse subset of foreground and mid-ground objects across frames 1–3 and detects nothing at all in the hallway in frames 4–5. In frame 1, it segments the dog (bottom-left, ~1.2 m away, facing left/upward toward the camera wearer), a white floor box right beside the dog (~1 m away, near arm's reach), a wooden chair (~2 m away, behind and above the box), and the seated person (~2 m away on the right, facing away and to the right toward the desk with hands in reach of the desktop, partly occluded at the top edge). In frames 2 and 3, as the camera wearer turns right and steps back to ~2.5–3 m while the person turns their head toward the camera in frame 3, only the potted plant near the center-right window (~2 m away) and an adjacent windowpane on the right are segmented. While the masks in frame 1 help separate the overlapping boundaries between the dog, the white box, and the person's silhouette against the cluttered floor and dark desk, the segmentation map is highly unreliable overall. It mislabels the white floor box in frame 1 as a 'laptop' and the bright windowpanes in frames 2 and 3 as a 'tv', completely misses the seated person in frames 2 and 3, and fails to detect the desks, actual monitors, walls, and doors across all five frames.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is entirely blank in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, providing a single yellow body skeleton only in the center of frame 3 where the person is seated at the office desk roughly 2.5–3 m in front of the retreating camera wearer. In frame 3, the detected head keypoints cluster on the left side of the skeleton while the shoulders and torso extend downward and to the right, indicating that the person's body is angled toward the desk while their head is turned over their left shoulder toward the camera wearer, with their arms extending rightward within reach of the desk surface. This skeletal overlay reveals the exact limb and torso articulation of the seated person in frame 3, which is almost completely hidden in the underexposed, shadowed lower half of the RGB image. However, the pose map is severely unreliable across the sequence because it fails to detect the seated person in frames 1 and 2 (where their head is partially cropped at the top of the frame and their back is turned), misses all magenta hand keypoints even where the person's hands rest on the desk in frames 1–3, and mistakes the dark desk and chair geometry in frame 3 for a horizontally splayed torso and legs.
